MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron carries almost no positive signal (its whole range is essentially negative), firing weakest/most negatively on prepositions and determiners that complete a fixed verb/adjective complement idiom ("appalled **at** the thought", "a bunch **of**", "as **a** fake", "think green **as** dull") and returning toward zero on ordinary mid-sentence function words and collocation completions ("hard **coded**", "spend that much **on**", "such **a** large", "**but**") — i.e. it is best described as a suppression unit for idiomatic preposition/determiner complements rather than a detector of a positive concept.

This neuron fires at the pivot token of a conversational hedge/concession — e.g. the "is" in "even though that **is** who she is" / "that **is** more or less…", the clause-final "though", and the comma right before a contrastive "but" — i.e. the point where an informal writer qualifies or concedes a previous statement; it is suppressed on ordinary noun/verb-phrase continuations ("these characters", "small portion", "to be done").
